title: 2026 Code Violations

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: 2026 Code Violations
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

copies of public records concerning municipal code-enforcement actions within the City of El Reno.

Specifically, I request a digital copy, spreadsheet, or log of all residential code-enforcement violations, citations, and notices issued from January 1, 2026, through the date this request is processed.

To limit clerical search time, please provide the information in its existing electronic format, such as Excel, CSV, or a text file. I am requesting only the following fields:

- Property owner’s or responsible party’s name
- Street address
- Violation type
- Date the violation was recorded or notice was issued

If the City does not maintain a centralized spreadsheet or log containing these fields, please provide the existing underlying electronic records from which this information can be extracted.

If any responsive record does not contain the property owner’s or responsible party’s name, please provide the remaining requested fields rather than withholding the entire record.

If the estimated cost will exceed $25, please provide an itemized estimate before processing the request. I request that any fees be waived because the records will be made available to the general public and concern the enforcement of municipal health, safety, and property-maintenance laws.

If any portion of this request is denied, withheld, or redacted, please identify the specific statutory exemption under the Oklahoma Open Records Act supporting that decision and release all reasonably segregable portions of the records.

Thank you for your attention and cooperation.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

title: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Auburn School District email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.subject: Confirmation - PRR#2026-066 - MuckRock
communications.communication:
Dear MuckRock/Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting,

This email acknowledges Auburn School District's receipt of your public records request dated October 5, 2026.

You requested the following documents:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com<mailto:*@mcminimeelaw.com>), exchanged with any Auburn School District email account, alias, or internal routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirely of the District's available archival retention window.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.520, the District estimates that it may be able to provide you with documents responsive to your request within thirty (30) business days (November 17, 2026).

The district will locate and assemble the information requested, notify third persons or agencies affected by the request if applicable, and/or to determine whether any of the information contained in such documents is exempt from public disclosure.

If additional clarification is needed, we will respond as quickly as questions arise.

To view the procedure and costs associated with Public Records click Board Policy 4040P<https://drive.google.com/open?id=1q0g-_-8x8bM__8Wuj8NkR1x7R5XMUMDU> . Below is a brief summary of potential fees:

  *   Photocopies or printed copies .15 cents per page
  *   Electronic records .10 cents per page for records scanned to an electronic format
  *   Five cents per every 4 electronic files or attachment uploaded to email, cloud-based data storage service, or other means of electronic delivery
  *   Ten cents per gigabyte for the transmission of public records in an electronic format or for the use of District equipment to send the records electronically
  *   Actual cost of any digital storage media or device provided by the District, the actual cost of any container or envelope used to mail the copies to the requestor, and the actual postage or delivery charge.
  *   The District may charge a flat fee of up to two dollars for any request as an alternative to fees when the agency reasonably estimates and documents that the cost allowed under this subsection are clearly equal to or more than two dollars.
  *   A customized service charge may be imposed if the District estimates that the request would require the use of information technology expertise to prepare data compilations, or to provide customized electronic access services when such compilations and customized access services are not used by the District for other District purposes. The customized service charge may reimburse the District up to the actual cost of providing the services.
  *   The District may choose to not calculate the actual costs it charges for providing public records if doing so would be unduly burdensome.
  *   The District may waive any charge assess for a request.

If requested, the District will provide a summary of the applicable charges before fulfilling the request. The requestor will be allowed to revise the request in order to reduce the applicable charges. A deposit of up to ten percent of the estimated costs may be required before processing the request.

The above timeframes are simply estimates and processing your request may take longer than predicted. If you have questions or concerns, feel free to call me at (253) 931-4900.

communications.subject: Records & Closed - PRR#2026-066 - MuckRock
communications.communication:
Dear MuckRock/Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting,

This email is about your public records request dated October 5, 2026.

You requested the following documents:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com<mailto:*@mcminimeelaw.com>), exchanged with any Auburn School District email account, alias, or internal routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirely of the District's available archival retention window.

**One record is attached. The attached document was an attachment to a responsive email.

Following a review of the records responsive to your public records request, the District has determined that all other responsive records are exempt from disclosure under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), 20 U.S.C. § 1232g, 34 CFR § 99.3, and RCW 42.56.230(1) and (2)(a)(iii), and RCW 42.56.230(7)(a).

All additional responsive records concern a single, identifiable student. FERPA protects personally identifiable information contained in student education records, including information that, alone or in combination with other information, could identify a student.

Given the specific nature of the request and the information contained in the responsive records, the District has determined that redaction of direct identifiers would not sufficiently protect the student's identity. Disclosure of the remaining information would still permit identification of the student and reveal information protected under FERPA.

Accordingly, the District is withholding the other responsive records in their entirety, as no reasonably segregable, nonexempt information can be disclosed without compromising the student's protected information.

**An exemption log is attached to this email.

**Your request is now closed.

OUTCOME
One record has been provided, attached to this email.
One record has been provided but all other records have not been provided as the District has determined that the responsive records are exempt from disclosure under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), 20 U.S.C. § 1232g, 34 CFR § 99.3, and RCW 42.56.230(1) and (2)(a)(iii), and RCW 42.56.230(7)(a).

**With this letter, the District closes its response to your October 5, 2026, public records request.

NOTICE
The Public Records Act's one-year statute of limitations to seek judicial review has started to run because the Auburn School District does not intend to disclose further records or further address the request. A statute of limitations is the deadline for initiating legal proceedings.

ACTION
If you have questions or concerns or believe additional responsive records have not been provided, please promptly contact me.

Please feel free to contact me any time.

Sincerely,

Lisa Connors
Assistant Director of Human Resources
Public Records Officer

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Travel authorizations, expense reports, receipts, and payment records, sufficient to show who paid for registration, travel, lodging, and meals (the City, the African American Mayors Association (AAMA), a company, or another third party), for the attendance of Mayor Van R. Johnson II and the staff of the Mayor's Office at:

AAMA annual conferences held in 2024, 2025, and 2026, and AAMA board or Corporate Business Council events; and
any event hosted or sponsored by Axon, Fusus, Flock Safety, or SoundThinking/ShotSpotter, including the Flock Safety Meet & Greet at Ruth's Chris Steakhouse on June 5, 2026, if anyone named above attended.

Please also include any gift, hospitality, or sponsored-travel disclosure, record, or acceptance involving any of those companies or AAMA, from January 1, 2020 through the date of this request. These records are likely held by Financial Services and the Mayor's Office; please search both. Please produce on a rolling basis.

If any part of this request cannot be released, please tell me which part and the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(d) provides, and release the rest. If there are no records for an item, please say so for that item. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

title: Jail Booking Log / Arrest Register (Jan 2025-Present)

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Jail Booking Log / Arrest Register (Jan 2025-Present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To the Custodian of Records, Webb County Sheriff's Office:

Under the Texas Public Information Act (Tex. Gov't Code ch. 552), I request the following existing records,
in the public interest and not for any commercial purpose (research and public education regarding local
detention practices). This is a new and distinct request from any prior request; it seeks the Office's
general jail arrest/booking log, not records pertaining to immigration detainees.

I request the Sheriff's Office **arrest and booking log** (the jail booking records the Office maintains in
the ordinary course) for every individual booked into the Webb County Jail from **January 1, 2025 to
the present**. For each booking, I request the existing fields your jail-management system records,
including:

1. Booking or system (SO) number;
2. Name;
3. Date and time of booking/confinement;
4. Date of release;
5. The charge(s) or hold(s) associated with the booking, as recorded in the charges field (including any
   notation your system enters for a hold or detainer);
6. Arresting/committing agency;
7. Warrant or reference number.

This is the Office's routine arrest/booking log -- the same public jail-booking information reflected in
your public inmate/booking search -- and I request it in the existing electronic format your jail-management
system exports (a spreadsheet, CSV, or delimited file is preferred; I do not require a formatted report). If
producing it requires programming or manipulation of data, § 552.231 requires a written statement of
whether it can be produced, in what form, and the cost and time -- and then production; every
jail-management system can export its booking log.

To be clear about scope: I am requesting the Office's general arrest/booking log for ALL bookings in this
period, which is public jail-booking information under the Act. I am NOT requesting records generated by or
for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, nor information about persons held on behalf of the Service;
any immigration-hold notation that appears in the booking-charges field is incidental booking data the
Office records for its own custody purposes, and does not make the general arrest/booking log confidential.
I do not seek any confidential criminal-history record; the SID number and any DPS criminal-history record
information may be withheld under § 411.083, which I concede.

As a public-interest, non-commercial request, I ask for a fee waiver or reduction; if fees will exceed $40,
please provide the itemized estimate required by § 552.2615 before incurring cost, and I will respond
promptly, including narrowing the date range if that helps. If the Office intends to withhold any
responsive information, it must timely request an Attorney General decision under § 552.301; absent a timely
request, the information is presumed public under § 552.302. Please also preserve all responsive records
pending resolution. Thank you.

Sincerely,
Glen Wasserstein
Immigration Law Group, P.C.
1717 K Street NW, Suite 900, Washington, DC 20006
glen@immigrationgroup.com | (929) 786-1863

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Glen Wasserstein

Under the Texas Public Information Act (Tex. Gov't Code ch. 552), I request the following existing records, 
in the public interest and not for any commercial purpose (research and public education regarding local 
detention practices). This is a new and distinct request from any prior request; it seeks the Office's 
general jail arrest/booking log, not records pertaining to immigration detainees. 

I request the Sheriff's Office **arrest and booking log** (the jail booking records the Office maintains in 
the ordinary course) for every individual booked into the Webb County Jail from **January 1, 2025 to 
the present**. For each booking, I request the existing fields your jail-management system records, 
including: 

1. Booking or system (SO) number; 
2. Name; 
3. Date and time of booking/confinement; 
4. Date of release; 
5. The charge(s) or hold(s) associated with the booking, as recorded in the charges field (including any 
notation your system enters for a hold or detainer); 
6. Arresting/committing agency; 
7. Warrant or reference number. 

This is the Office's routine arrest/booking log -- the same public jail-booking information reflected in 
your public inmate/booking search -- and I request it in the existing electronic format your jail-management 
system exports (a spreadsheet, CSV, or delimited file is preferred; I do not require a formatted report). If 
producing it requires programming or manipulation of data, § 552.231 requires a written statement of 
whether it can be produced, in what form, and the cost and time -- and then production; every 
jail-management system can export its booking log.

period, which is public jail-booking information under the Act. I am NOT requesting records generated by or 
for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, nor information about persons held on behalf of the Service; 
any immigration-hold notation that appears in the booking-charges field is incidental booking data the 
Office records for its own custody purposes, and does not make the general arrest/booking log confidential.

information may be withheld under § 411.083, which I concede.

communications.communication:
Thank you for contacting foipaquestions@fbi.gov.

Please check the status of your FOIPA Request at http://vault.fbi.gov by clicking on “Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request” on the right side of the page, and follow the instructions below.

Check the Status of Your FOIPA Request

If your FOIPA Number is [1195846-0] please enter [1195846-000] into the system. If your FOIPA Number is [1195846-1] please enter [1195846-001] into the system. If you have any questions about the status of your FOIPA request, please e-mail foipaquestions@fbi.gov.

FIND STATUS OF FOIPA- Request statuses are updated weekly

Please enter the whole FOIPA number-Example: [1234567-000]

FOIPA:
Results will show the Request Number, Case Type and Process Description shown below:
FOIPA:
1234567-000
Case Type:
FOIPA
Process Description (Will display the current progress of the request)

The FBI’s FOIPA Program is searching the FBI’s indices for potentially responsive documents.

You may be contacted via formal letter for all fees and/or negotiation issues that may apply.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Before you can check the status, you must have received correspondence assigning a FOIPA request number and the information transferred to the online database. Status information is updated weekly. If a request has been closed within the last six months the online database will display the following: The FOIPA number entered has been closed, and appropriate correspondence has been sent to the address on file.

Estimated Dates of Completion
Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system, and the FBI receives a voluminous amount of requests on a daily, weekly, monthly, and annual basis.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Our complex requests are further divided into small (51-250 pages), medium (251-500 pages), large (501-4,999), and extra-large (over 5,000 pages) sub-tracks.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  The more potentially responsive pages a request has, the more complex it becomes, greatly increasing the time required for processing. Generally, the larger the file, the longer it takes to process.

Currently, simple track cases average approximately 122 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Complex requests in the small processing track are currently averaging 360 days from the date of receipt for processing, those in the medium processing track are currently averaging 1,230 days, those in the large processing track are currently averaging approximately 2,010 days, and those in the extra-large track are averaging 2,370 days.

Respectfully,

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Fusus Contracts, Manuals, Audit Logs
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All contracts, licenses, MOUs, MOAs, data agreements, letters of intent, State of Work documents, Scope of Work documents, and other agreement documents with Axon and Fusus that were active any time between 1/1/2025 and the date this request is fulfilled.
2. User manuals, handbooks, or comparable instructional documents provided to the department by Fusus regarding Fusus products and services
3. The complete audit logs/audit trails for the Fusus platform from 1/1/2025 until the date this request is processed. I request the listing be provided in Excel format so I can easily sort/filter it. Redactions should be done in Excel.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Rose Terse

communications.subject: RE: Washington Public Records Act Request #P001993-083026
communications.communication:
Hello,

I am writing to appeal your complete redaction of the Audit-export-1791404435451_R.pdf file you provided in the first installment of records.

The redaction reads "Pursuant to Section 5 of Washington State Senate Bill 6002, 'automated license plate reader data is not subject to disclosure under the public records act, chapter 42.56, except such data may be used for bona fide research as defined in RCW 42.48.010 and does not include individually identifiable information.'"

RCW 10.130.020(2) defines audit trail data as "all forms of data collected or generated by an automated license plate reader system that identify how the system is accessed or used", including "information about who accesses or uses the system, and how and when the system is accessed or used." Crucially, it states that audit trail data "does not include automated license plate reader data", explicitly differentiating it from ALPR data. As such, the prohibitions around sharing ALPR data in RCW 10.130.050 do not apply to the audit data you have redacted.

I ask again that you provide the full breadth of records I have requested, without improper redactions without further unnecessary delay.

Thank you,
Rose

title: De Baca County Jury Summons List Request

communications.subject: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act Request: De Baca County Jury Summons List Request
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The following materials regarding the compilation and composition of the master jury list:

All reports, databases, spreadsheets, or equivalent materials regarding the jury summons process within the last 4 years. Please include the total number of individuals who were summoned, responded, and who were selected to a jury summons.

In the event that there are any fees for obtaining or copying these records, please inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. Should the fees exceed $100, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees as I am requesting the information on behalf of a 501(c)(3) nonprofit and the disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest and will contribute significantly to the public’s understanding of how master jury lists are created. This information is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If possible, please provide the requested documents electronically. However, if this is not feasible, please inform me of the available methods for obtaining these records. Further, if you expect a significant delay in responding to this request, please contact me with information concerning when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific exemption that justifies the refusal to release the information and notify me of the appeal procedures available to me under the law.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within the timeframe required by the statute.

Sincerely,
Angel Carter

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Angel Carter

communications.subject: Re: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act Request: De Baca County Jury Summons List Request
communications.communication:
Dear Angel:

It is the policy of the 10th District Court to be fully responsive to all 
requests for public records available under the Inspection of Public 
Records Act, NMSA 1978, § 14-2-1 et seq. (“IPRA”). We have received your 
Email dated November 3, 2026, requesting that the court provide 

*“*The following materials regarding the compilation and composition of the 
master jury list:

All reports, databases, spreadsheets, or equivalent materials regarding the 
jury summons process within the last 4 years. Please include the total 
number of individuals who were summoned, responded, and who were selected 
to a jury summons.*”*  

We have searched our files and made inquiries within our court and have 
determined that the records that you are seeking are not in the possession, 
custody, or control of the court.  Instead, we believe that the custodian 
of the records that you are requesting is Administrative Office of the 
Courts .  Therefore, pursuant to NMSA 1978, § 14-2-8(E), we will be 
forwarding your request to that agency’s records custodian   
ipra.aoc@nmcourts.gov   for further response.  In addition, you may want to 
contact that records custodian to directly convey your public records 
request to that agency.

 

Sincerely,

On behalf of Records Custodian

communications.subject: Re: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act Request: De Baca County Jury Summons List Request
communications.communication:
Dear Angel Carter,

The Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) has received your records 
request dated November 3, 2026 as forwarded to the AOC from the Tenth 
Judicial District "regarding the jury summons process within the last 4 
years."  All responsive information regarding the jury process in the New 
Mexico Judiciary is located on the Court's website 
here: https://jury.nmcourts.gov/

Regarding your request for "the total number of individuals who were 
summoned, responded, and who were selected to a jury summons." The AOC does 
not have responsive records to this request. IPRA does not require a public 
body to create documents, lists, spreadsheets, statistics or other reports 
in order to respond to a records request. IPRA does not require public 
bodies to answer questions, compile information or data into a document, 
run reports, or create any new record. NMSA 1978, § 14-2-8(B) (“Nothing in 
the Inspection of Public Records Act shall be construed to require a public 
body to create a public record.”).

 Thank you on behalf of

Karl Reifsteck, Records Custodian

The Administrative Office of the Courts

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: 2026 Brady List (Pierce County Prosecuting Attorney)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All current "Brady lists" and "Giglio lists" (per Brady v. Maryland/Giglio v. United States) maintained by your office, along with accompanying potential impeachment material.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Rose Terse

Adrian McDaniel

Good morning,

I can send the records to you in GovQA, an online public records portal that you can access through Pierce County’s webpage: https://www.co.pierce.wa.us/5446/Online-Public-Records-Request-Portal. You can access the invoices in “My Request Center” using your email address 201089-59367203@requests.muckrock.com and select “forgot password” to create your own password.  You will then be able to view the records.

In my previous letter to you dated June 30, 2026, I indicated that it will take until July 30, 2026, to complete the process for your next installment of records. We are still on track for completion of the review for records within that time frame. I will contact you upon completion of the review to inform you of the results.

Thank you,
Adrian McDaniel
Public Records Officer
Pierce County Prosecuting Attorney

RE: PIERCE COUNTY Prosecuting Attorney PUBLIC RECORDS REQUEST, Reference # P041339-010526. 
 
Dear Rose Terse, 
A production of records responsive to your request is ready for release. These records meet the fee threshold, as outlined in Pierce County Code 2.04.030(E). Please see the attached invoice, INV26-P041339-5. 
 
To make a payment online, log back into your Pierce County Public Records Request portal account and select "View My Invoices". Select "Make a Payment" for this invoice and follow the prompts to enter your payment information. (https://u8387778.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.VEsWrlMiJDg0mXafq1mEXXndrKlkWAcXKs3RKk0x6-2B8pdCk0ipTOgEFrezx8dJEGTEGSWYfnvF8UlMzIRC67G-2BfU3pkPbhhu86G19FienkUzJeTLf3Wh6ipnaLWflqnq2Q2vSDVkavEiXYzyby6S43YxpWOfFDYeLU-2BC8CZGwVWRuvZ-2FJbCEjlDiyWLk-2F9VvHCgNWPTwfTwYy9oubLU52g-3D-3DlLVz_cZC2DE3u2cs2QgRIye4LE-2FUuF21C7Nw2WTsI40J0tkEB7tIy1FyNVop12O496qbghtbzawlLBdX57vx3EgqRGJ-2FSQXH-2BvX0TS0mf0COOhjRNAqhQVj7qc6N2xRxKe-2B22qPDubp36IG7g6qc-2BKKJcC45QMrxPLvxUzHA4xt-2BLf7qQPsOuUIF6eOh1-2Fb5fKOtBcAi7-2FVk0TLH9sDDQsT-2Bi4HJY36k0L-2BJX4t7xapulc-2BcLm5DBWEah48gYJWSC8OTLC3gFooA-2BYZi5Vv3h5w1VQT-2BUqWPjD1VTXSX8x77BRbII6KbuFNtkgjHzYNz3MN5vzb0-2BvcjCLkm1Te1eVEV006Ue5VNpmY2C2THfKl7-2Frmk0K6URUXXxKKl89VVHGy-2FFkdt2OTnMdf-2FQA6y-2BYkkgOg-3D-3D)

If no reference number is noted, we may not be able to determine which request to apply the payment. For cash payments, exact change is required. Personal checks will not be accepted as a method of payment. Cashier checks or money orders must be made payable to Pierce County. Processing of payment may take up to one business day, regardless of method of payment. 
Responsive records will be released to you upon completion of processing of payment. Pursuant to RCW 42.56.120(4) and Pierce County Code 2.04.040(J) if you do not pay the deposit or any installment payment due for the requested copies within 30 calendar days after receiving this notice, by the due date on the invoice, this agency may stop providing further installments of records and close the request.

Prosecuting Attorney

RE: PIERCE COUNTY Prosecuting Attorney PUBLIC RECORDS REQUEST, Reference # P048347-101526. 
 
Dear Rose Terse, 
A production of records responsive to your request is ready for release. These records meet the fee threshold, as outlined in Pierce County Code 2.04.030(E). Please see the attached invoice, INV26-P048347-1. 
 
To make a payment online, log back into your Pierce County Public Records Request portal account and select "View My Invoices". Select "Make a Payment" for this invoice and follow the prompts to enter your payment information. 
Alternatively, you may remit your payment to the Pierce County address on your invoice. Please include a copy of the invoice or note the Reference Number of the request with your payment so that we may apply your payment to the appropriate request. If no reference number is noted, we may not be able to determine which request to apply the payment. For cash payments, exact change is required. Personal checks will not be accepted as a method of payment. Cashier checks or money orders must be made payable to Pierce County. Processing of payment may take up to one business day, regardless of method of payment. 
Responsive records will be released to you upon completion of processing of payment. Pursuant to RCW 42.56.120(4) and Pierce County Code 2.04.040(J) if you do not pay the deposit or any installment payment due for the requested copies within 30 calendar days after receiving this notice, by the due date on the invoice, this agency may stop providing further installments of records and close the request. 
 
Respectfully, 
Prosecuting Attorney

communications.subject: Re: Washington Public Records Act Request #26-2427
communications.communication:
Our office does not accept advance payments for public records requests. If you prefer not to mail a check, you may submit payment electronically through GovQA, an online public records portal that you can access through Pierce County’s webpage: https://www.co.pierce.wa.us/5446/Online-Public-Records-Request-Portal. A GovQA account has been set up using your email address to allow you to view the invoices and submit payments.  You can access the invoices in “My Request Center” using your email address 201089-59367203@requests.muckrock.com and select “forgot password” to create your own password.  You will then be able to view the invoices and make payments.

Please remit $0.30 by mailing cash, money order, or a certified check in the exact amount due to 930 Tacoma Ave S Rm 946, Tacoma, WA 98402; or making the payment in the Pierce County public request portal (GovQA). Please note that we cannot make change for you. Personal checks are not accepted.  Any money order or certified check received that is not made payable to “Pierce County” will be returned to you and may result in closing out the request due to non-payment. These records are also available for you to review in person at no cost to you.  If you would like to review the records in person, please contact me at 253-798-4149 or via email at PAOpublicrecords@piercecountywa.gov to schedule a time to do so.

Please be advised, if payment for the first installment is not received by Monday, November 23, 2026, your request will be deemed abandoned as of that same date. In that event this agency will provide no further response to your record request due to the abandonment of it. The Public Records Act’s one-year statute of limitations to seek judicial review will start to run as of that same date. If your request is abandoned on that date, due to non-payment, you may ask us follow up questions for a period of up to thirty days thereafter. If you have any questions, believe we have somehow misunderstood your request, or wish to clarify your request, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Thank you,
Adrian McDaniel
Public Records Officer
Pierce County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office

title: Dayton Open Records Request- Eviction Data

communications.subject: Ohio Open Records Law Request: Dayton Open Records Request- Eviction Data
communications.communication:
Dear Open Records Coordinator,

I am writing on behalf of the Data Acquisition Lab to formally request access to public records under the Ohio Open Records Law, §149.43 et seq. We are requesting local eviction information for data visualization and analysis, which will enable a more meaningful understanding of community-level housing and displacement trends. We plan to request this information on a quarterly basis going forward.

I am specifically requesting the following information related to eviction filings in the City of Dayton, spanning from January 1st, 2026 to present:
• Case Number
• Case Type
• Court Date
• Filed Date
• Reason for Eviction Filing (i.e., nonpayment of rent, lease violations, etc.)
• Hearing Date
• Hearing Time
• Case Disposition (if applicable)
• Plaintiff Name
• Plaintiff Address
• Plaintiff City
• Plaintiff Zip
• Plaintiff Phone Number
• Defendant Name
• Defendant Address
• Defendant Address Unit
• Defendant City
• Defendant Zip
• Defendant Phone Number
• Monthly Rent (monthly contracted rent amount)
• Amount Owed by the Defendant (if applicable)
• Subsidy Amount Received, if Available (i.e., government subsidy for rent -- like from a voucher)

If possible, please provide the dataset as a .CSV file, with one row per case, including the above fields, and notify me in advance of any necessary clarification or related costs exceeding $100.

If certain records or portions of records are exempt from disclosure, please provide a written explanation of the specific exemption(s) and release any non-exempt portions of the requested records.

Thank you for your attention to this request. If you have any questions or require further information, please feel free to contact me.

Implementation Checklist for DOJ OIP Guidance on “Still-Interested” Inquiries
1.	Ensure there are reasonable grounds to make a “still-interested” inquiry in first instance.
2.	Absent good cause, do not make multiple “still-interested” inquiries.
3.	Use requester’s preferred method of communication and in the absence of a preference, communicate by telephone or email as the default. 
4.	Memorialize any decision by a requester to withdraw a request that is conveyed by telephone by sending the requester a brief email or letter noting the withdrawal.
5.	Provide requesters no less than thirty (30) working days to respond to the “still-interested” inquiry and ensure that there is a simple way to do so.

7.	Prior to administratively closing a request based upon the lack of a response by the requester, make good faith efforts to reach out to the requester using multiple methods of communication.

LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF FOIA 

1.	The definition of “records” includes:
“[A]ill books, papers, maps, photographs, machine readable materials, or other documentary materials, regardless of physical form or characteristics, made or received by an agency of the United States Government under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business and preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the Government or because of the informational value of data in them.”  44 U.S.C. § 3301 (emphasis supplied).
2.	FOIA requires that “each agency, upon any request for records which (i) reasonably describes such records and (ii) is made in accordance with published rules stating the time, place, fees (if any), and procedures to be followed, shall make the records promptly available to any person” 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(3)(A).
3.	FOIA requires that “each agency shall establish a system to assign an individualized tracking number for each request received that will take longer than ten days to process and provide to each person making a request the tracking number assigned to the request” 5 U.S.C. § 522(a)(7)(A).
4.	FOIA requires that each agency shall “establish a telephone line or Internet service that provides information about the status of a request to the person making the request using the assigned tracking number, including the date on which the agency originally received the request; and an estimated date on which the agency will complete action on the request. 5 U.S.C. § 522(a)(7)(B).
5.	FOIA also requires federal agencies to make a final determination on FOIA administrative appeals that it receives within twenty days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) after the receipt of such appeal, unless the agency expressly provides notice to the requester of “unusual circumstances” meriting additional time for responding to a FOIA request. 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(ii).
6.	FOIA expressly provides that a person shall be deemed to have constructively exhausted their administrative remedies if the agency fails to comply with the applicable time limitations provided by 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(I) - (ii). See also 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(C).
7.	FOIA provides that any person who has not been provided the records requested pursuant to FOIA, after exhausting their administrative remedies, may seek legal redress from the Federal District Court to enjoin the agency from withholding agency records and to order the production of any agency records improperly withheld from the complainant.

communications.subject: FOIA Expedited Processing Disposition Reached for NARA-NGC-2022-000788
communications.communication:
Your request for Expedited Processing for the FOIA request NARA-NGC-2022-000788 has been 
			denied. 
		Additional details for this request are as follows: 
 
  * Request Created on:
					02/18/2022 
  * Request Description:
					Please See attachment for description. 
  * Expedited Processing Original Justification:
					I am seeking expedited processing. In any denial of my request for expedited processing the Agency must state in detail how my request does not meet requirement and who, by name, was involved in the denial determination. 
1. The subject is of widespread and exceptional media interest and the information sought involves possible questions about the government's integrity that affect public confidence. 
a. U.S.C § 552(k)(6)(B) requires the full Council, not just the co-chairs. Did OGIS announce the meeting as the full Council and notify all in the same manner as other Council meetings Per FOIA. “Not less frequently than annually, the Council shall hold a meeting that shall be open to the public and permit interested persons to appear and present oral and written statements to the Council.” This meeting did not meet those requirements. 
b. There was no such a meeting per 5 USC § 552(k)(6)(B) in 202, 2020, 2019, etc. 
c. The February 2, 2022 stealth Chief FOIA Officers Council meeting was not advertised in the normal way for such meetings and was not posted on either the NARA or DOJ websites (DOJ ma have posted the day before). this meeting was so poorly advertised and not posted in advance to the OGIS or DOJ OIP websites. 
d. The meeting was not on You Tube for public viewing and preservation. I have not seen that before for a FOIA open meeting. 
e. Federal Register Notice 01/20/2022 says, “Additional details about the Chief FOIA Officers Council and the meeting, including the agenda, are available on OGIS's website.” This was false. 
f. Chief FOIA Officer and FOIA Advisory Committee meetings are typically 3 hours not 1 hour. 
g. Comments were limited to 5 min per requester. 
h. I have been in contact with multiple members of the media regarding these matters, both before and after the meeting, There is exceptional interest in Saving FOIA Part II. 
i. OGIS and DOJ OIP intentionally did not address my questions submitted in advance of the meeting and during the meeting into the online chat. This appears to be a violation of law. 
j. DOJ and NARA continue to hold unlawful meetings. FOIA Improvement Act states, “Not later than 10 business days before a meeting of the Council, notice of such meeting shall be published in the Federal Register.” Not done for the Nov17, 2021 meeting. ?OGIS: For Nov17, 2021 meeting oral comments were limited to 3 minutes, even though 15 minutes were allocated and I continued to call in. Why the limitation and why was I not recognized a 2nd time? 

2. There is a reasonable expectation of an imminent loss of a substantial due process rights in connection with statutory times for FOIA actions. 
a. OGIS and DOJ OIP intentionally did not address my questions submitted in advance of the meeting and during the meeting into the online chat. This appears to be a violation of law affecting my due process rights in connection with open FOIA meetings. 

3. Information is urgently needed to inform the public concerning some actual or alleged government activity/malfeasance. 
a. See paragraph 1 above. 
b. I am an individual primarily engaged in dissemination of information via extensive email lists, blogs, coordination with Open Government Advocate Organizations and members of the media. 

In any denial of my request for expedited processing, I am seeking that the Agency identify who, by name and email was consulted and that the Agency provide specific justification as to how my request stated herein does not qualify. 

STILL-INTERESTED PREEMPTIVE REPLY. This is a preemptive reply to the Justice Department guidelines the procedure known as a “still interested” inquiry, through which a FOIA officer can confirm that the requester has not lost interest in obtaining the documents. 
  * Expedited Processing Disposition Reason:
					After carefully reviewing your request, we do not believe expedition is warranted, as you have not demonstrated that your request meets the above-referenced criteria.  Specifically, you have not provided evidence that there is an urgent need to inform the public of a government activity, or widespread and exceptional media interest involving questions affecting public confidence in the Government’s integrity that can be addressed by the records you seek.  You also have not provided evidence that there is a reasonable expectation of any imminent loss of a substantial due process rights in connection with the statutory times of FOIA actions with the records you seek.  If you are not satisfied with our action on your request for expedited processing, you have the right to file an administrative appeal in writing by mail or email.  If by mail, please address your appeal to the Deputy Archivist (N), National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Rd., College Park, Maryland 20740. Both the letter and the envelope should be clearly marked “Freedom of Information Act Appeal.” If by email, please submit your appeal to FOIA@nara.gov addressed to the Deputy Archivist.  Your appeal should be received within 90 calendar days of the date of this denial, and it should explain why you think this response does not meet the requirements of the FOIA. 
If you would like to discuss our response before filing an appeal to attempt to resolve your dispute without going through the appeals process, you may contact our FOIA Public Liaison Gary M. Stern for assistance via email at garym.stern@nara.gov. 
You may also contact the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS), the Federal FOIA Ombudsman’s office, which offers mediation services to help resolve disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies. The contact information for OGIS is noted below: 
Email:  ogis@nara.gov  Website:  ogis.archives.gov 
Tel:  202-741-5770 or 1-877-684-6448

communications.communication:
NARA's responses have nothing whatsoever to do with the records I am seeking. 
Therefore, I am seeking FPL dispute resolution from Gary Stern to this FOIA request.
RECORDS SOUGHT VIA FOIA.

NARA 22-U.R.MUCK. OGIS ADR +Chief FOIA Officers Meeting 2 Feb 2022
See PDF. See Requested Format.

Background.

1. By emails from foiacompliance@gmail.com of January 16, 2022, Subject: Chief FOIA Officers Council Meeting February 2, 2022, 1400 EST, I notified several hundred Chief FOIA Officers and FOIA Professionals of said meeting and further stated:

Please pay particular attention to the attached Public Comment, “Mandatory Right to OGIS Dispute Resolution (20220116).” Your agency is likely citing unlawful language, potentially as the result of previously disseminated errant OGIS guidance as OGIS may have sought to minimize workload due to grossly inadequate funding for mediation (and FOIA compliance oversight).

2. On January 16, 2022 6:54 PM I nest that same email (Attachment A) to ogisopenmeeting@nara.gov; alina.semo@nara.gov; bobak.Talebian@usdoj.gov; kirsten.mitchell@nara.gov; Vanita.Gupta19@usdoj.gov; debra.wall@nara.gov; martha.murphy@nara.gov; sheela.portonovo@nara.gov; carrie.mcguire@nara.gov; teresa.brady@nara.gov; dwaine.bacon@nara.gov; jessica.hartman@nara.gov; christa.lemelin@nara.gov; garym.stern@nara.gov.

3. OGIS Director, recently stated (contrary to law and OGIS/DOJ model language policy), “Agencies have the option to include either or both the FPL and OGIS in adverse determinations.”

4. NARA, DOJ, and agencies across the Federal Government have been citing unlawful language wrt OGIS dispute resolution requiring requesters to contact the Agency FPL first:

“If you are unable to resolve your FOIA dispute through our FOIA Public Liaison, the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS), the Federal FOIA Ombudsman’s office, offers mediation services to help resolve disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies.”

Requested Records.

I am respectfully seeking as individual files records in NARA’s custody only from January 15 2022 to present records related to said January 16, 2022 emails and any emails or other OGIS or DOJ correspondence relating to OGIS dispute resolution services as follows:

1. Records of receipt, forwarding and replies to the January 16, 2022 6:54 PM email from foiacompliance@gmail.com Subject: Chief FOIA Officers Council Meeting February 2, 2022, 1400 EST.
2. Records of receipt, forwarding and replies to any emails received from FOIA Officers or other party regarding any January 16, 2022 email from foiacompliance@gmail.com Subject: Chief FOIA Officers Council Meeting February 2, 2022, 1400 EST.
3. Records of any emails from OGIS or DOJ OIP to Chief FOIA Officers, FOIA professionals or others discussing the right to OGIS dispute resolution, mediation or assistance, FPL dispute resolution or assistance, and/or OGIS or DOJ model language regarding OGIS/FPL assistance, mediation, or dispute resolution services.
4. I am also seeking a copy of this FOIA Request, which is an Agency record subject to that exists and is in the Agency’s possession at the time of my FOIA request. This record is a responsive record integral to my Request. Release of the Agency’s copy is not optional.

NOTE: To the extent that you contend that any records are exempt, you must identify the specific records and release all segregable portions. I may seek an in-camera inspection in any court proceeding. This is a simple request.

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Norwood Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

title: Initial-contract (CBM) cases and their outcomes, October 1999 to present

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Initial-contract (CBM) cases and their outcomes, October 1999 to present
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please include all cases with N-Category "Initial Contract" (Case Type CBM) opened or received from October 1, 1999 through the date the search is run, whatever the case's status or reason for closing. That means cases closed with "Agreement Reached" and also, for example:

- "Parties Failed to Respond"
- "Case Cancelled"
- "Question re: Representation"
- "Employees Included In/Folded Into Existing Unit"
- "Facility Closed"
- "Other"
- cases with no reason for closing recorded
- cases still open

My earlier request FOIA-2022-00042 was fulfilled with only cases closed as "Agreement Reached".

For this request I am asking that cases which did not reach agreement can be counted.

Fields. For each case, please provide the following, where they exist. Field names are from the extract produced for FOIA-2022-00042:
1. The FMCS case number or other unique case identifier
2. Received Date; Initiated Date; the date the case was closed
3. Case Type; N-Case Type; N-Category; N-Case Source (for example F-7 from Union, F-7 from Organization, NLRB, FLRA)
4. N-Date Submitted, and any identifier linking the case to its F-7 notice
5. The NLRB case number (for example 13-RC-123456), or the certification date, for cases opened from NLRB certifications
6. Basis for Closing (Case Statistics)
7. Contract Agreement Date
8. Employer; Union; Union Local; bargaining unit size (BU)
9. The employer's location and the affected or bargaining-unit location (city, state, ZIP code)
10. The industry code (NAICS), if recorded
11. Whether a mediator held joint or separate meetings, and the number and dates of those meetings, if recorded

Personal information. To make processing easier, you may leave out the names, telephone numbers and email addresses of individual employer and union contacts. I do not need them. Please do not leave out the employer or union names.

Older records. If cases from before a particular year are in a legacy system, or have fewer fields, please provide whatever is available for those years, and tell me which fields or years are missing rather than withholding the rest.

Format. I would like the records as a spreadsheet or delimited text file (.xlsx or .csv), one row per case, in the form the system exports. If producing all years would take much longer, please send each portion as it becomes ready, starting with the most recent years.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Forest Gregg

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #FOIA-2027-00003
communications.communication:
Thank you for your letter. 

I request a waiver of all fees. If the waiver is denied, I agree to pay fees up to $100, and I ask that you contact me before incurring anything higher. I am not a commercial requester. I ask to be placed in the "all other requesters" fee category, which includes two hours of search time and 100 pages (or the electronic equivalent) at no charge. Because I am asking for an electronic export of existing records, I expect duplication costs to be minimal.

Fee waiver request

Disclosure is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government, and it is not primarily in my commercial interest. 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii).

1. The records concern identifiable operations of the government. The records document one specific FMCS program. Under 29 U.S.C. § 173 and Section 8(d) of the National Labor Relations Act, FMCS offers mediation to parties bargaining a first contract. Since about 2003, it has opened those cases partly from certifications the NLRB sends it. The records show:
- which newly certified units FMCS opened cases for;
- how long the cases lasted;
- how each case was closed: agreement reached, parties failed to respond, facility closed, or otherwise.

These are FMCS's own records of how it carries out a statutory duty.

2. The records are meaningfully informative and not already public. FMCS publishes F-7 notice data, but it does not publish the outcomes of its initial-contract cases. My earlier request, FOIA-2022-00042, produced only the cases closed as "Agreement Reached". The public therefore sees FMCS's successes but not its full caseload.

The only published study using comparable FMCS case records covers 1999–2004 (Ferguson, Industrial and Labor Relations Review, 2008), and those records are not public. Using the public F-7 and NLRB data alone, I have found that only about a third of units newly certified since 1999 later show a renewed contract. Public data cannot show whether the rest never reached a first contract, reached one and lost it, or never had an FMCS case at all. The requested records answer that question directly.

Policy researchers have pointed to this gap. A 2026 Economic Policy Institute report observes that the role of employer-side law firms in "frustrating workers' attempts to reach a first contract has largely gone unexamined" (Poydock, Wiggin and McNicholas 2026). FMCS's case records are the only systematic federal record of what happens in first-contract bargaining.

3. Disclosure will reach a reasonably broad audience, and I have the ability and expertise to deliver it. Since 2021, I have maintained labordata (https://labordata.bunkum.us/), a free public warehouse of 15 federal labor datasets. It includes NLRB case and election records, FMCS F-7 notices and work-stoppage data, voluntary recognitions, OSHA and Wage and Hour enforcement records, and Department of Labor union and employer disclosure filings. It needs no login, and offers a web interface, an API, CSV export and direct database queries.

It is heavily used. Over the most recent three months, labordata answered roughly 48,000 data queries, after excluding automated crawlers, from more than 300 distinct client applications. It also receives a few thousand browser visits a month. Its users include:
- university researchers;
- a labor-watchdog nonprofit that queries it daily;
- union researchers
- labor-relations consultants;

In a single recent week, users connected from the networks of at least seven universities, including UCLA, NYU and Penn State.

Researchers and policy organizations rely on it:
- Pezold, Jäger and Nüss, "Labor Market Tightness and Union Activity" (NBER Working Paper 31988, 2023), measures strikes using the FMCS work-stoppage data I collected and published.
- The Economic Policy Institute's 2026 report on employer spending on union avoidance, which examines the firms involved in "the stalling of first contract negotiations", uses NLRB data from labordata and cites it as a source (Poydock, Wiggin and McNicholas 2026).

I will release these records on labordata, free of charge and with documentation, joined to NLRB election records so that each case can be traced to the certification that started it. I will also publish an analysis of first-contract outcomes by year, industry and region.

Linking FMCS case records to NLRB certifications takes specialized knowledge of both agencies' data. I have already built that linkage for the F-7 notices, so the public will get usable information rather than a raw extract.

4. The contribution to public understanding will be significant. No public source today says how often FMCS's first-contract cases end in agreement, or how many newly certified units FMCS reaches at all. Timely first contracts are a matter of active national policy debate. The PRO Act, for example, would establish "a bargaining process for reaching a first contract in a timely manner", with FMCS mediation and arbitration (Poydock, Wiggin and McNicholas 2026). Evaluating such proposals requires knowing how FMCS's existing first-contract program performs. These records would provide the first public measure of that in two decades.

5. The request is not primarily in my commercial interest. I have no commercial interest in these records. labordata is noncommercial, and everything it publishes is free.

If FMCS grants only part of the waiver, I ask for a waiver of whatever portion of the fees qualifies. If the waiver is denied, I agree to pay fees up to $100, and I ask that you contact me before incurring anything higher.

Sincerely,
Forest Gregg

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is focused on Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) and Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEX), both are products of LexisNexis Risk Solutions (LNRS / RELX). We are making this request because we found evidence that your agency likely uses, has access to, or contributes data to AVCC (directly or indirectly). If your agency has no relationship with these products, please tell us so.

We are seeking records that indicate whether your agency contributes data to AVCC/PSDEX, and if so, what other agencies have access to that data. 
--
We are requesting the following records:
1) All signed contracts, addendums, amendments, or agreements between your agency and LexisNexis that are currently in effect or were in effect at any point between 1/1/2020 and the date this request is fulfilled.  
[CONTEXT] Common documents include "AVCC XML Addendum" / "Schedule A" / "Master Terms & Conditions" / "sub-agency agreements" / "joinder agreements" or other similar agreements. If your agency contributes data or gets AVCC access through a consortium or fusion center, please include the MOU or similar agreement outlining that AVCC relationship. 
2) AVCC Usage Logs. 
 - 2.A) If your agency shares data with AVCC/PSDEX, please provide query logs of who has accessed your agency's data and what reason/case number they provided while searching your agency's records. We understand some of these reports are generated by LexisNexis rather than stored locally; please include any such report your agency has received or can obtain. Please provide in CSV or XLSX format where available. If you are unable to see logs of how your agency's data is used by other agencies within AVCC, please indicate so. 
3) AVCC Configuration:
 - 3.A) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing 
 - 3.B) Configuration Explainer Documents: Typically documents with details on what data LexisNexis recommends that you contribute, and what they recommend you exclude. Sometimes this may be called "FAQs and FYIs for Exclusions", or may include integration suggestions for an interface with your RMS/JMS/CAD systems. 
--
PRIORITY: The two most important documents we seek are your signed AVCC XML Addendum and 3.A. - The AVCC agency configuration page printout. 
SEARCH TERMS: To aid in your search, we recommend the following search terms: "AVCC" "Accurint" "PSDEX" "Public Safety Data Exchange" "Public Safety Marketplace" and "Accurint Virtual Crime Center"

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

Re: Public Information Request of June 11, 2026, Reference # R188897-061126; 
Dear Shawn Segal, 
The Austin Police Department received a public information request from you on June 11, 2026 to request copies of records pertaining to the following: “:To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records: 

This request is focused on Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) and Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEX), both are products of LexisNexis Risk Solutions (LNRS / RELX). We are making this request because we found evidence that your agency likely uses, has access to, or contributes data to AVCC (directly or indirectly). If your agency has no relationship with these products, please tell us so. 

We are seeking records that indicate whether your agency contributes data to AVCC/PSDEX, and if so, what other agencies have access to that data. 
-- 
We are requesting the following records: 
1) All signed contracts, addendums, amendments, or agreements between your agency and LexisNexis that are currently in effect or were in effect at any point between 1/1/2020 and the date this request is fulfilled. 
[CONTEXT] Common documents include "AVCC XML Addendum" / "Schedule A" / "Master Terms & Conditions" / "sub-agency agreements" / "joinder agreements" or other similar agreements. If your agency contributes data or gets AVCC access through a consortium or fusion center, please include the MOU or similar agreement outlining that AVCC relationship. 
2) AVCC Usage Logs. 
- 2.A) If your agency shares data with AVCC/PSDEX, please provide query logs of who has accessed your agency's data and what reason/case number they provided while searching your agency's records. We understand some of these reports are generated by LexisNexis rather than stored locally; please include any such report your agency has received or can obtain. Please provide in CSV or XLSX format where available. If you are unable to see logs of how your agency's data is used by other agencies within AVCC, please indicate so. 
3) AVCC Configuration: 
- 3.A) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing 
- 3.B) Configuration Explainer Documents: Typically documents with details on what data LexisNexis recommends that you contribute, and what they recommend you exclude. Sometimes this may be called "FAQs and FYIs for Exclusions", or may include integration suggestions for an interface with your RMS/JMS/CAD systems. 
-- 
PRIORITY: The two most important documents we seek are your signed AVCC XML Addendum and 3.A. - The AVCC agency configuration page printout. 
SEARCH TERMS: To aid in your search, we recommend the following search terms: "AVCC" "Accurint" "PSDEX" "Public Safety Data Exchange" "Public Safety Marketplace" and "Accurint Virtual Crime Center" 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Shawn Segal
